feedback.problem:
$$

Consider the curve $x\operatorname{cos}⁡y=2.$ Given that $x=x(t),\text{ }y=y(t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6$ on the curve at the point $(4,\frac{\pi }{3}),$ find the value of $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}$ at that point. Do not round the answer.

$\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}=$
{{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x\operatorname{cos}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y-x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡y\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting the given information $\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=6,$ $x=4,$ and $y=\frac{\pi }{3},$ and solving for $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡y-x\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡y\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 6\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})-4\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 6\cdot \frac{1}{2}-4\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ 3-2\sqrt{3}\cdot \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =0 \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
